title: rhodanthemum gayanum subsp. antiatlanticum
intro: Rhodanthemum gayanum subsp. antiatlanticum, commonly known as the Atlantic White Hawk's Beard, is a plant species in the daisy family that is native to the Atlantic coast of Morocco and Western Sahara. The Atlantic White Hawk's Beard has been traditionally used in folk medicine to treat various ailments, offering potential health benefits such as anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties. The plant's therapeutic actions are attributed to its ability to reduce inflammation, modulate the immune system, and exhibit antioxidant activity, which may contribute to its use in treating conditions like wounds, infections, and respiratory issues. The bioactive constituents of Rhodanthemum gayanum subsp. antiatlanticum include sesquiterpene lactones, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
